about.what: Source paragraphs and task selections for the Word Studio v2 benchmark (#85).
about.author: Written for this benchmark by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) in a Pari session on 2026-10-16. Not user text and not copied from any essay corpus.
about.voice: Plain student voice with a small vocabulary (good, bad, big, a lot, shows, hard), so the tasks look like the writing Pari is for.
about.quotes: Every quotation comes from a public-domain work and is listed on its paragraph. Paragraphs about copyrighted books describe the plot and quote nothing.
about.sentence_index: Task field 's' is the 1-based index into 'sentences'. 'select' must occur once in that sentence as a whole-word match unless 'occurrence' says which one.

sentences: Many schools are thinking about banning phones during class, and I think this is a good idea.
When students have their phones out, they get distracted really easily and stop listening to the teacher.
A lot of kids say they only use their phones to check the time, but most of the time they are actually on social media.
In my opinion, I think that a ban would help students do better on tests because they would pay attention more.
Some parents are worried that they will not be able to reach their kids in an emergency.
However, the school office can always call a parent if something bad happens.
Overall, a phone ban is a good way to make classrooms better places to learn.

paragraphs.topic: Atticus Finch in To Kill a Mockingbird
sentences: In To Kill a Mockingbird, Atticus Finch shows that doing the right thing is not always easy.
He agrees to defend Tom Robinson even though he knows that most people in Maycomb will be angry at him.
Atticus is someone who never gives up on what he believes, even when his own children get bullied at school because of it.
He tells Scout that you never really understand a person until you look at things from their point of view.
This shows that he wants his kids to be fair to everyone, not just people who are like them.
Atticus is a good example of a person who stays brave when it would be easier to stay quiet.

tasks.select: someone who never gives up on what he believes

sentences: The printing press was one of the most important inventions in history.
Before Johannes Gutenberg built his press around 1440, books had to be copied by hand, which took a really long time.
Because of this, books were very expensive and only rich people and churches could have them.
After the press was invented, books could be made much faster and for a lot less money.
More people started learning how to read, and new ideas spread across Europe quickly.
Some historians say that the press helped cause big changes like the Reformation and the Scientific Revolution.
Without it, the world we live in today would probably be very different.
Teenagers need about eight to ten hours of sleep every night, but most of them get a lot less.
One reason is that their body clocks change during puberty, so they do not feel tired until late at night.
On top of that, many teens stay up looking at their phones, and the blue light makes it even harder to fall asleep.
Not getting enough sleep is bad for the brain because it makes it hard to remember things and focus in class.
It can also make teens more moody and stressed out.
Scientists have found that students who sleep more usually get better grades.
This is why some experts think schools should start later in the morning.
When my family moved to the United States, I was eleven years old and I only knew a few words in English.
The first few months at school were really hard because I could not understand what the teachers were saying.
I felt alone most of the time, and I was too scared to talk in class.
My English teacher, Ms. Alvarez, started staying after school to help me with reading and writing.
She never made me feel stupid when I made mistakes.
Little by little, I started to understand more and even make some friends.
Now I am the one who helps new students when they first get here, because I know how it feels.
Social media has a big effect on how teenagers see themselves.
On apps like Instagram and TikTok, people usually only post the best parts of their lives, like vacations and nice clothes.
When teens look at these posts all day, they start to compare themselves to others and feel bad about their own lives.
A survey from 2023 found that almost half of teens said social media made them feel worse about their bodies.
Social media is not all bad, though, because it also helps people stay in touch with friends and find others with the same interests.
Still, I believe that teens should limit how much time they spend on these apps.

tasks.select: the best parts of their lives

quotes.text: a tale told by an idiot

sentences: In Macbeth, Shakespeare shows how wanting power too much can destroy a person.
At the start of the play, Macbeth is a loyal soldier who fights bravely for King Duncan.
After the witches tell him he will be king, he cannot stop thinking about it.
Lady Macbeth pushes him to kill Duncan, and he finally agrees even though he feels guilty.
Once he becomes king, he keeps killing people because he is afraid of losing what he has.
By the end, Macbeth says that life is "a tale told by an idiot," which shows how empty he feels.
His story is a warning about what happens when ambition gets out of control.

paragraphs.topic: a first job at a pizza restaurant
sentences: Last summer I got my first job working at a small pizza restaurant near my house.
At first I thought it would be easy, but I quickly found out that it was a lot of work.
On busy nights we had to make dozens of pizzas in just a few hours, and customers got upset if their food was late.
My manager, Tony, taught me how to stay calm and do one thing at a time.
I also learned how to talk to people who were angry without getting angry myself.
The job was tiring, but it showed me that I can handle stress better than I thought.
These skills will help me in college and in any job I have in the future.
Some people think school uniforms are a bad idea, but I think they help students in many ways.
First, uniforms make it harder for kids to judge each other based on how much their clothes cost.
When everyone wears the same thing, students from poor families do not stand out as much.
Second, uniforms save time in the morning because students do not have to pick out an outfit every day.
Critics say that uniforms take away students' freedom to express themselves.
However, students can still show who they are through their hobbies, their writing, and the way they treat others.

paragraphs.topic: the green light in The Great Gatsby

quotes.work: F. Scott Fitzgerald, The Great Gatsby (1925), chapter 9
quotes.license: public domain in the United States

sentences: In The Great Gatsby, the green light at the end of Daisy's dock stands for Gatsby's dream of being with her again.
Gatsby stretches out his arms toward the light across the water, which shows how badly he wants something that is far away.
The light is also connected to the bigger idea of the American Dream, the belief that anyone can become rich and happy if they work hard enough.
By the end of the novel, Gatsby's dream falls apart, and the light seems to lose its meaning.
Nick says that Gatsby "believed in the green light," even though the future he wanted kept moving away from him.
Fitzgerald uses the light to show that some dreams are impossible to reach.

paragraphs.topic: child labor in the Industrial Revolution
sentences: During the Industrial Revolution, a lot of children worked in factories and mines instead of going to school.
Some of them were only six or seven years old, and they often worked twelve hours a day.
The conditions were very dangerous, and many children got hurt by the machines or became sick from breathing in dust.
Factory owners liked hiring kids because they could pay them less money than adults.
Over time, reformers wrote articles and gave speeches about how bad the situation was.
In Britain, the Factory Act of 1833 finally set limits on how many hours children could work.
Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria, and they have saved millions of lives since they were discovered.
The problem is that bacteria can change over time so that the medicine does not work on them anymore.
This happens faster when people take antibiotics they do not really need, like for a cold, which is caused by a virus.
It also happens when people stop taking their pills early because they start to feel better.
If this keeps going, simple infections could become deadly again.
To stop this, doctors need to be careful about giving out antibiotics, and patients need to finish the whole treatment.
My grandmother is the person who has had the biggest impact on my life.
She grew up on a farm in Mexico and never got the chance to finish school, but she is one of the smartest people I know.
Every Sunday she cooks a huge meal for the whole family, and she makes everyone put their phones away so we can actually talk.
She taught me that being kind is more important than being right.
When I was having a hard time in middle school, she was the one who listened to me without judging.
I want to be the kind of person who makes others feel welcome, just like she does.
Some school districts have switched to a four-day school week to save money and give students more time to rest.
Supporters say that teachers are less tired and students come to school more ready to learn.
The extra day off can also be used for doctor appointments, jobs, or family time.
However, the longer school days can be hard for younger kids who have trouble focusing for that long.
Working parents might also have to pay for childcare on the fifth day, which could be a problem for families without much money.
Before more districts make this change, they should look closely at how it affects students' learning.

paragraphs.topic: the shared dream in Of Mice and Men
sentences: In Of Mice and Men, George and Lennie share a dream of owning a small farm together.
For George, the dream gives him a reason to keep working hard even though his life is lonely.
For Lennie, it is mostly about getting to take care of rabbits.
Most of the other workers on the ranch have no one, so they are surprised that the two men travel together.
Steinbeck uses their friendship to show how important it is to have someone who cares about you.
When the dream falls apart at the end, it shows how hard it was for poor workers to change their lives during the Great Depression.
The Montgomery Bus Boycott was a key event in the civil rights movement.
It started in December 1955 when Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her seat to a white passenger.
In response, Black residents of Montgomery stopped riding the city buses for more than a year.
Many people walked miles to work every day or set up carpools so that they would not have to use the buses.
The boycott hurt the bus company because it lost most of its riders.
In 1956, the Supreme Court ruled that segregation on buses was unconstitutional, and the boycott ended in victory.
Bees are very important for the food we eat.
When a bee goes from flower to flower to collect nectar, it carries pollen that helps plants make fruits and seeds.
About one third of the food crops in the world depend on bees and other pollinators.
In the past few decades, bee populations have gone down a lot because of pesticides, disease, and the loss of wild flowers.
If bees keep disappearing, foods like apples, almonds, and blueberries could become much harder to grow.
People can help by planting flowers and avoiding chemicals in their gardens.
Joining the robotics team in tenth grade was one of the best choices I ever made.
Our first competition was a disaster because our robot stopped working in the middle of the match.
I felt embarrassed, and I wanted to quit the team right then.
Instead, our coach told us to figure out what went wrong and try again.
We spent weeks testing every part until we found a loose wire in the motor.
At our next competition, the robot worked perfectly and we made it to the finals.
That experience taught me that failing is just part of getting better.
Standardized tests like the SAT are supposed to measure how ready students are for college, but they do not tell the whole story.
A student's score can depend a lot on whether their family could pay for tutoring and practice books.
Some students are also very nervous test-takers, so their scores do not show what they actually know.
Because of this, more than 1,800 colleges have made the SAT optional.
I think colleges should look at grades, essays, and activities instead of focusing on one test score.

quotes.work: William Shakespeare, Romeo and Juliet, Act 2 Scene 3

sentences: Romeo and Juliet is often called a love story, but it is also a story about how acting too fast can lead to disaster.
Romeo and Juliet meet, fall in love, and get married in less than a week.
Neither of them stops to think about what their families will do when they find out.
Friar Laurence even warns Romeo that "they stumble that run fast," but Romeo does not listen.
When Romeo hears that Juliet is dead, he kills himself right away instead of waiting to learn the truth.
If the two young lovers had slowed down, the play might have had a happy ending.
The Black Death was a plague that spread across Europe starting in 1347.
It was carried by fleas that lived on rats, and it moved quickly along trade routes and through crowded cities.
Within just a few years, it killed somewhere between a third and half of Europe's population.
Because so many workers died, the people who survived could ask for higher pay, which made the old feudal system weaker.
The plague also made a lot of people question the church, since prayers did not seem to stop the disease.
Coral reefs are some of the most beautiful places on Earth, but they are in serious trouble.
When the ocean gets too warm, corals push out the tiny algae that live inside them and give them their color.
This is called coral bleaching, and if the water stays hot for too long, the coral can die.
Reefs are home to about a quarter of all ocean species, so losing them would hurt a lot of sea life.
They also protect coastlines from big waves during storms.
Cutting down on pollution and greenhouse gases is the best way to give reefs a chance to recover.
Some people believe the voting age should be lowered from 18 to 16.
At sixteen, many teenagers already have jobs, pay taxes, and can drive a car.
Laws about schools, the environment, and the economy will affect young people for the rest of their lives, so they should have a say in them.
Critics argue that sixteen-year-olds are not mature enough to make good choices about politics.
However, studies of places like Austria, where sixteen-year-olds can vote, show that young voters make choices that are just as thought-out as older voters.

quotes.text: I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend.

sentences: In Frankenstein, Mary Shelley shows that the creature becomes a monster because of how he is treated.
When he is first created, the creature is gentle and wants to be loved.
However, every person who sees him is scared of his appearance and attacks him or runs away.
Even Victor Frankenstein, the man who made him, abandons him right after bringing him to life.
The creature says, "I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend."
This line shows that his anger comes from being rejected over and over, not from his nature.
The Dust Bowl was a period in the 1930s when huge dust storms hit the Great Plains.
Farmers had plowed up the grass that held the soil in place, and then a long drought dried everything out.
When strong winds came, they picked up the loose dirt and created clouds of dust so thick that people could not see the sun.
Crops died, animals got sick, and many families lost their farms.
Thousands of people packed up their belongings and moved west to California looking for work.
The disaster taught the government that it needed to help farmers protect the land.
Every Saturday for the past two years, I have volunteered at a food bank in my neighborhood.
At first, I only went because I needed community service hours for school.
But after a few weeks, I started to really care about the people who came in.
Many of them were working parents who just did not have enough money at the end of the month.
One woman told me that the food we gave her was the only reason her kids had dinner that week.
Hearing that made me realize how many people in my own town are struggling.
Now I want to study social work so I can help families like hers.
Plastic bags are cheap and easy to use, but they cause big problems for the environment.
Most of them are only used once before they get thrown away.
Because they are so light, they often blow out of trash cans and end up in rivers and oceans, where animals like sea turtles mistake them for food.
A plastic bag can take hundreds of years to break down.
Several states, such as California and New York, have already banned single-use plastic bags.
I think every state should do the same and encourage people to bring reusable bags to the store.

paragraphs.topic: the loss of order in Lord of the Flies
sentences: In Lord of the Flies, a group of boys stranded on an island slowly lose their sense of right and wrong.
At first, they choose Ralph as their leader and try to follow rules, like only speaking when they hold the conch shell.
As time goes on, Jack becomes more interested in hunting than in keeping the signal fire going.
More and more boys join Jack's tribe because it seems more fun than doing chores.
By the end, the boys have turned violent, and two of them are dead.
Golding uses the story to suggest that people can quickly become savage when there are no rules to control them.

paragraphs.topic: women's suffrage in the United States
sentences: The fight for women's right to vote in the United States lasted for more than seventy years.
It officially began at the Seneca Falls Convention in 1848, where activists like Elizabeth Cady Stanton demanded equal rights for women.
For decades, suffragists gave speeches, marched in parades, and even went to jail for their cause.
Many people at the time thought that women were too emotional to make decisions about politics.
Finally, in 1920, the 19th Amendment was passed, which gave women the right to vote.
This victory showed that ordinary people can change the law if they keep pushing for it.
Vaccines work by teaching the immune system how to fight a disease before a person ever gets sick.
They contain a weak or harmless piece of a germ, which the body learns to recognize.
If the real germ shows up later, the immune system can attack it quickly.
Thanks to vaccines, diseases like smallpox have been wiped out, and polio is almost gone.
When enough people in a community are vaccinated, it also protects those who cannot get the shot, like newborn babies.
This is called herd immunity.
Many students say they have too much homework, and I agree that it can sometimes do more harm than good.
After a full day of classes, students still have to spend three or four hours on assignments every night.
This leaves them with very little time for sports, family, or sleep.
Some homework is helpful because it lets students practice what they learned in class.
But when teachers give busywork just to fill time, students get tired and stop caring about learning.
Schools should set limits on homework so that it is useful and not overwhelming.
In The Crucible, Arthur Miller shows how fear can make a whole town turn against itself.
When a group of girls in Salem start accusing people of witchcraft, the adults believe them without asking for proof.
Anyone who disagrees with the court is in danger of being accused too.
John Proctor knows the girls are lying, but at first he is afraid to speak up because he has his own secret.
In the end, he chooses to die rather than sign a false confession.
Miller wrote the play in the 1950s to criticize the way people were being accused of being communists without real evidence.
Since my mom works night shifts at the hospital, I have been taking care of my little brother after school since I was thirteen.
I help him with his homework, make him dinner, and make sure he goes to bed on time.
Some days it is stressful, especially when I have a big test the next morning.
But taking care of him has made me more patient and responsible than most kids my age.
I have learned how to manage my time and stay calm when things do not go as planned.
My brother looks up to me, and that makes all the hard work worth it.
College athletes bring in millions of dollars for their schools, but for a long time they were not allowed to earn any of it.
Big football and basketball programs sell tickets, jerseys, and TV rights, while the players who make it all possible get nothing except a scholarship.
Many athletes spend more than forty hours a week on their sport, which makes it hard to keep a part-time job.
In 2021, new rules finally let athletes make money from their name and image.
I think this was a fair change, and schools should go even further by sharing some of their profits with players.
On July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the moon.
The Apollo 11 mission was the result of years of hard work by thousands of scientists, engineers, and astronauts.
The United States wanted to beat the Soviet Union in the space race, which was part of the larger Cold War.
Millions of people around the world watched the landing live on television.
The mission showed what humans can do when they work together toward a big goal.
It also led to new technologies that we still use today.
Renewable energy comes from sources that do not run out, like the sun, wind, and water.
Unlike coal and oil, these sources do not release a lot of greenhouse gases when they make electricity.
In the last ten years, the cost of solar panels has dropped so much that solar power is now cheaper than coal in many places.
One problem is that the sun does not always shine and the wind does not always blow, so we need better batteries to store the energy.
Even with these challenges, switching to renewable energy is one of the best ways to slow down climate change.
In Animal Farm, George Orwell uses a story about farm animals to show how power can corrupt leaders.
After the animals take over the farm, they promise that all animals will be treated the same.
Over time, the pigs start giving themselves special privileges, like sleeping in beds and drinking alcohol.
Napoleon uses his dogs to scare anyone who questions him, and he changes the rules whenever it helps him.
By the end, the other animals cannot tell the difference between the pigs and the humans.
Orwell was warning readers that a revolution can end up with the same problems it was trying to fix.

paragraphs.topic: coming back from a knee injury
sentences: During my junior year, I tore a ligament in my knee during a soccer game and had to miss the rest of the season.
Soccer had always been a big part of who I was, so not being able to play made me feel lost.
For the first few weeks, I barely wanted to leave my room.
Then my physical therapist pushed me to set small goals, like walking without crutches or doing ten squats.
Every small win gave me a little more confidence.
When I finally stepped back onto the field the next fall, I was stronger, both physically and mentally.

paragraphs.topic: fast food ads aimed at children
sentences: Fast food companies spend billions of dollars every year on ads that are aimed at children.
These commercials often use cartoon characters, bright colors, and free toys to make kids want to eat there.
Young children cannot always tell the difference between an ad and a regular TV show, so they believe what the ads say.
This is a problem because eating too much fast food can lead to health issues like obesity and diabetes.
I believe the government should put stronger limits on food ads that target kids, the same way it does for cigarette ads.
The Silk Road was not one single road but a network of trade routes that connected China to the Middle East and Europe.
Merchants traveled these routes for more than a thousand years, carrying goods like silk, spices, and paper.
But the Silk Road did more than move products from one place to another.
It also helped spread religions, languages, and inventions between very different cultures.
For example, Buddhism traveled from India to China along these routes.
In many ways, the Silk Road was an early example of how the world is connected.
Every year, millions of tons of plastic end up in the ocean.
Over time, sunlight and waves break this plastic into tiny pieces called microplastics.
These pieces are so small that fish and other sea animals eat them by accident.
Scientists have even found microplastics in drinking water, salt, and human blood.
We still do not fully understand how they affect our health, but some studies suggest they could cause inflammation.
Reducing how much plastic we use is the most important step we can take to fix this problem.

paragraphs.topic: Greasers and Socs in The Outsiders
sentences: In The Outsiders, Ponyboy learns that people are more alike than they seem.
At the start of the novel, he believes that the Socs, the rich kids from the west side, have perfect lives with no problems.
Then he meets Cherry Valance, a Soc girl who tells him that rich kids have troubles too.
Later, Randy, another Soc, admits that he is tired of all the fighting between the two groups.
These conversations make Ponyboy realize that the line between Greasers and Socs is not as clear as he thought.
S. E. Hinton shows that judging people by their group keeps us from seeing who they really are.

paragraphs.topic: the causes of World War I
sentences: World War I had many causes, but the event that started it was the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in 1914.
Before that, the major powers of Europe had already been building up their armies and making alliances with each other.
These alliances meant that a fight between two countries could quickly pull in many others.
When Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, Russia came to Serbia's defense, and then Germany, France, and Britain joined in.
Nationalism also played a big role, because many people were proud of their countries and eager to prove their strength.
Artificial intelligence tools like chatbots are becoming common in schools, and teachers are not sure how to handle them.
Some teachers worry that students will use AI to write their essays and never learn how to think for themselves.
Others believe AI can be a useful tutor that explains hard ideas in a simple way.
In my experience, AI is most helpful when I use it to check my understanding, not to do the work for me.
Schools should teach students how to use these tools honestly instead of banning them completely.

quotes.text: To be, or not to be

sentences: Hamlet is a character who thinks too much and acts too little.
After his father's ghost tells him that Claudius murdered him, Hamlet promises to get revenge.
But instead of acting right away, he spends most of the play doubting himself and planning.
In his famous speech, he asks, "To be, or not to be," as he wonders whether life is worth the pain.
Even when he has a perfect chance to kill Claudius while he is praying, he decides to wait.
His delay ends up causing the deaths of many people, including himself.
Most people know that exercise is good for the body, but it is also good for the brain.
When we exercise, our hearts pump more blood to the brain, which brings it extra oxygen.
Studies have shown that regular exercise can improve memory and help people focus.
It can also lower stress and make people feel happier because the body releases chemicals called endorphins.
Even a short walk of twenty minutes can make a difference.
For students, this means that taking breaks to move around might actually help them study better.

paragraphs.topic: being the first in the family to apply to college
sentences: I will be the first person in my family to go to college, and that comes with a lot of pressure.
My parents did not have the chance to continue their education because they had to start working when they were teenagers.
They have always told me that school is the key to a better life.
Filling out applications was confusing because no one at home had done it before, so I had to ask my counselor for help with almost every step.
Even though the process was hard, it made me more determined to succeed.
I want to make my parents proud and show my younger cousins that college is possible for them too.
Some people think public libraries are not needed anymore because everything is online, but I strongly disagree.
Libraries give free internet and computers to people who cannot afford them at home.
They also offer programs like reading groups for kids, job help for adults, and English classes for immigrants.
For many people, the library is one of the only safe and quiet places where they can study.
If cities cut library funding, the people who would be hurt the most are the ones who already have the least.
That is why we should keep supporting our libraries.
